security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, when emulating a CHERI capability load (e.g., CLC) through an authorizing capability that grants R and C but lacks LM, the emulator checks the capability tag read FROM MEMORY (or the pre-authorization tag) to decide whether to strip W and LM, rather than checking the tag of the finalized capability being WRITTEN INTO THE DESTINATION REGISTER after bounds/authority checks have completed. If authorization clears the tag (e.g., bounds violation, representability failure), a QEMU implementation checking the memory tag would strip W/LM from a now-untagged value, whereas hardware would skip stripping because the written-back tag is 0.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: tag check on source/memory tag instead of destination/writeback tag before LM/W permission stripping in capability load emulation (e.g., if (mem_ctag) vs if (result_ctag) before clearing CAP_PERM_WRITE | CAP_PERM_LOAD_MUTABLE)
security_spec.summary: Capability load LM/W permission stripping must gate on the written-back (post-authorization) tag, not the memory tag; using the pre-authorization tag can cause permission stripping on already-invalidated capabilities, diverging from hardware behavior

findings.finding: scountinhibit_pred now correctly checks menvcfg.CDE before allowing access to scountinhibit. Before this fix, scountinhibit was accessible even when menvcfg.CDE=0, violating the spec requirement that CDE=0 must raise an illegal-instruction exception. The fix adds the missing gate: if (!get_field(env->menvcfg, MENVCFG_CDE)) return RISCV_EXCP_ILLEGAL_INST. This matches the existing CDE-gating pattern already used for scountovf (line 1625) and sireg* indirect access (line 2769). The read/write paths (read_scountinhibit, write_scountinhibit) correctly mask through env->mcounteren, enforcing the delegated-bits-only access pattern per spec.

spec_citations.excerpt: [#norm:ssccfg_illegal_scountinhibit_cde0]#When `menvcfg`.CDE=0, attempts to access `scountinhibit` raise an illegal-instruction exception.# [#norm:ssccfg_illegal_scountinhibit_vs_vu]#When Supervisor Counter Delegation is enabled, attempts to access `scountinhibit` from VS-mode or VU-mode raise a virtual-instruction exception.#

findings.finding: MENVCFG_CDE is included in the write mask for both menvcfg and menvcfgh write handlers (lines 3183 and 3241), gated on cfg->ext_smcdeleg. Writes to CDE are properly constrained by the mask — only bit 60 is writable when smcdeleg is present. No side-effects (TLB flush, FENCE.I) are triggered by CDE changes, which is correct per spec (CDE only gates CSR accessibility, no microarchitectural state implications).
findings.snippet:
uint64_t mask = MENVCFG_FIOM | MENVCFG_CBIE | MENVCFG_CBCFE |
                    MENVCFG_CBZE | MENVCFG_CDE;

findings.finding: read_scountinhibit masks through env->mcounteren, returning only bits delegated by M-mode. write_scountinhibit similarly ANDs the write value with env->mcounteren before delegating to write_mcountinhibit. This correctly enforces the non-delegated bits as read-only zero per spec, preventing S-mode from writing inhibit bits for counters not delegated to it.

spec_citations.excerpt: [#norm:ssccfg_scountinhibit_nondelegated_ro]#For counters not delegated to S-mode, the associated bits in `scountinhibit` are read-only zero.#

findings.finding: This upstream qemu/qemu repository contains zero CHERI capability emulation code. Grep for cheri, CAP_PERM, load_mutable, PERM_WRITE, PERM_LOAD_MUTABLE, CLC, cap_load, writeback tag across target/ returned no matches. No cheri*.c, cheri*.h, or cap*.c files exist. The security spec's vulnerability pattern (checking source/memory tag instead of destination/writeback tag before stripping W/LM permissions in authorized capability loads) cannot be evaluated here because there is no code to evaluate. CHERI emulation lives in downstream forks (CHERIoT-Platform/qemu, CTSRD-CHERI/qemu). The PR's title 'Reword to clarify that load LM permission clearing is based on written back tag' appears to describe a different codebase — this branch only modifies a scountinhibit CDE check.
findings.snippet: N/A — no CHERI capability load emulation code exists in this repository
